title: Add tiered batching perf jobs (fast/standard/cost_efficient) with p95 regression gates
author: Rina Kobayashi
release_notes: Perf-canary now benchmarks batching_tier={fast,standard,cost_efficient} across top models and blocks merges on p95 latency regressions beyond tier-specific thresholds.
body:
## Summary
This adds a new perf-canary suite that runs our standard workload corpus against the tiered batching profiles (fast / standard / cost_efficient) for a small set of “top models” and GPU SKUs, and fails the PR if p95 latency regresses beyond tier-specific thresholds.

This is intended to catch scheduler / batching mapping changes early (especially tail latency and streaming cadence regressions) before we roll tier defaults behind the runtime feature flag.

## Why
We’ve been landing a series of runtime changes related to tiered batching defaults (ENG-18421) and new queue delay / batch formation metrics (ENG-18422). The existing perf-canary jobs cover “default config” only; with tiering, the “default” meaning changes by route/model/workload. We need explicit coverage of each tier to:
- prevent p95 regressions (fast tier in particular),
- make sure cost_efficient improvements don’t come with unacceptable tail-latency blowups,
- have a single place to compare tiers on the same workload for go/no-go.

## What’s included
- New `tiered_batching` suite definition which expands matrix dimensions:
  - `batching_tier`: `fast`, `standard`, `cost_efficient`
  - `model`: initial allowlist (see below)
  - `gpu_sku`: A10 + L4 (hosted-like), and H100 for “ceiling” coverage
  - `route`: `chat` + `completions` (embeddings are tracked separately; not gated in this PR)
  - `workload_profile`: `short_prompts`, `mixed`, `long_context` (derived from our canonical prompt bucketization)
- Regression gates:
  - p95 end-to-end latency (non-streaming) and p95 time-to-first-token (streaming)
  - tier-specific thresholds (more strict for `fast`, looser for `cost_efficient`)
  - comparison is against last-successful baseline on `main` for the same (model, sku, route, workload_profile, tier)
- Artifact + reporting:
  - uploads JSON + CSV summary tables per job
  - posts a compact tier comparison table in the GitHub Checks summary
  - keeps raw run logs as an artifact for tail debugging

## Initial model / SKU coverage
This is intentionally small to keep runtime and CI costs reasonable.

Models (initial allowlist):
- `llama-3.1-8b-instruct`
- `qwen2.5-7b-instruct`
- `mistral-small-instruct` (internal registry name)

GPU SKUs:
- `l4-24gb`
- `a10-24gb`
- `h100-80gb` (nightly + optional on PRs touching scheduler code)

## Thresholds
Thresholds are configured in `configs/regression_thresholds/tiered_batching.yaml`:
- fast:
  - p95 latency regression budget: +5%
  - p95 TTFT regression budget: +5%
- standard:
  - p95 latency regression budget: +8%
  - p95 TTFT regression budget: +8%
- cost_efficient:
  - p95 latency regression budget: +12% (we expect queueing)
  - p95 TTFT regression budget: +10%

Notes:
- These are relative-to-baseline gates only; absolute p95 targets remain in the SRE SLO docs.
- We also enforce a minimum sample size and will mark the gate as “inconclusive” (does not fail) if we don’t meet it due to infra flakiness.

## Implementation details
- Adds a `TieredBatchingJobBuilder` that expands the matrix and injects runtime config:
  - request metadata includes `batching_tier` and `streaming` flags
  - runner forwards tier into the runtime config payload used by the benchmark driver
- Updates baseline selection logic to include tier dimension (prevents incorrectly comparing `fast` results to `standard` baseline).
- Adds a “warmup only” phase per job to avoid first-run kernel cache noise (esp. on L4).
- Updates the Markdown checks summary to show:
  - p50/p95/p99, throughput, token/s, and failure rate
  - per-tier deltas vs baseline

## Files / areas changed
- `suites/tiered_batching.yaml` (new)
- `configs/regression_thresholds/tiered_batching.yaml` (new)
- `src/jobs/tiered_batching_builder.py` (new)
- `src/runner/baselines.py` (baseline key expanded)
- `src/reporting/checks_summary.py` (tier table)
- `workflows/perf-canary.yml` (new job group + path filters)
- `docs/suites.md` (documents tiered suite + interpretation)

## Example output (Checks summary excerpt)
Tier comparison (llama-3.1-8b-instruct, l4-24gb, chat, mixed):
- fast: p95 0.92s (Δ +1.9%) ✅
- standard: p95 1.04s (Δ +0.6%) ✅
- cost_efficient: p95 1.21s (Δ -3.8%) ✅

## Testing
- Ran locally against a sampled baseline file to validate the new baseline-key shape.
- Ran in CI using `--dry-run` matrix to validate workflow generation.
- Ran full suite once on staging runners (links in CI summary).

## Rollout / follow-ups
- This PR adds gating on L4/A10. H100 is enabled on nightly, and on PRs labeled `runtime-scheduler` (path filter: `src/runner/**` + label opt-in). We can adjust once costs are stable.
- Follow-up: add embeddings tier coverage once the runtime tier mapping stabilizes for embedding routes (tracked in ENG-18423 comments).

## Review notes / discussion
**Grace Kim (review):** The “mixed” workload bucket includes some long-context outliers. Can we cap context length for the L4 jobs to reduce variance?
**Rina Kobayashi (author):** Done. Added `max_input_tokens` cap for L4/A10 only; H100 keeps uncapped mixed bucket for sensitivity.

**Sahana Iyer (review):** CI cost seems high with full matrix on every PR. Can we add path filters + limit to one model unless scheduler code is touched?
**Rina Kobayashi (author):** Added path filters + default subset (llama + qwen) on PRs; full model set runs nightly. Scheduler-touch path filter triggers full set.

**Sofia Ivanova (review):** For streaming, TTFT is good, but we’ve been bitten by token cadence regressions. Any signal here?
**Rina Kobayashi (author):** Added an optional cadence check (p95 inter-token gap) but left it non-gating for now; shows as a warning in summary. We can promote to gating once stable.

**Sean Gallagher (review):** Please align threshold naming with SRE docs (fast/standard/cost_efficient) and include a note that these are CI gates, not customer SLOs.
**Rina Kobayashi (author):** Updated docs + config comments; clarified “regression gate” language.

## CI
Checks:
- lint: PASS
- unit-tests: PASS
- workflow-gen: PASS
- tiered-batching (L4/A10 subset): PASS
- nightly tiered-batching (H100): scheduled (not required for merge)

## Merge
Squash-merged to `main` after approvals. Baselines will populate automatically after first successful `main` run; expect “inconclusive (no baseline)” for the first 1–2 merges.
